knowledge.content: Task constraint: Only modify /app/user.cpp - do not modify any other files in the system
System has two libstdc++ versions: Debug at /usr/local/gcc-custom-debug/ (no optimizations), Release at /usr/local/gcc-custom-release/ (with optimizations). Modified in-house compiler.
Compiler libstdc++ source code location: /build/ directory
Requirement: No memory leaks detected by Valgrind
Problem: Program crashes in RELEASE mode but works in DEBUG mode

File structure: main.cpp has CustomHeapManager (bump allocator, 10MB heap), global new/delete operators overridden, Application class with init()/run()/shutdown() lifecycle, Monte Carlo π estimation. user.cpp has empty user_init(), user_cleanup(), user_main() functions.

Critical code pattern: Application destructor calls shutdown() which destroys g_custom_heap and sets it to nullptr. Global delete operator checks g_custom_heap - if null, calls std::free(), else calls custom deallocate(). Custom deallocate() does nothing (bump allocator).

Suspected bug: Objects allocated via custom heap during Application lifetime may have destructors that run AFTER shutdown() sets g_custom_heap=nullptr. These destructors would then call std::free() on memory from the custom heap buffer (not malloc'd), causing crash. Likely triggered by optimizer in release mode.

status: Step 2: Read source files. Identified CustomHeapManager pattern and likely object lifetime issue. Next: compile and run both modes to reproduce crash, then fix in user.cpp.
